title: Pre-Apprenticeship as an On-Ramp
description: How to use pre-apprenticeship to move job seekers, especially youth and people with barriers, into Registered Apprenticeship. Covers quality pre-apprenticeship design, funding through ITAs when on the ETPL, counting youth pre-apprenticeship toward the 20 percent work experience requirement, and stipends under WSD23-08.
notes: Audience: Youth providers, case managers. Format: LV. Hours assumed from format (LV = 3 hours).
learning_objectives: Identify the elements of a quality pre-apprenticeship with a direct link to a registered program.
Fund pre-apprenticeship through WIOA Adult, Dislocated Worker, or Youth.
Count youth pre-apprenticeship toward work experience requirements.
Design a warm handoff from pre-apprenticeship to apprenticeship.

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: What Makes a Quality Pre-Apprenticeship; Funding Pre-Apprenticeship Through WIOA; Youth Pre-Apprenticeship and Work Experience; Designing the Warm Handoff. There is no separate project lesson; each lesson ends in a practice exercise built on the same running case. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (LV; LV = 3 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Prerequisites reflect track order: APP 101 (Registered Apprenticeship for Workforce Professionals).
